Lending.name: DDM
Lending.reason: DMM (DeFi money market) DMG public-sale participants lost funds to Telegram impersonators/scammers off-chain; no protocol exploit, just social-engineering losses reimbursed by the foundation.

Lending.name: Armor.Fi
Lending.reason: Armor.Fi team members were scammed off-chain via a fake OTC deal; the loss was team tokens defrauded through social engineering, not a lending-protocol exploit.

Lending.name: Pinecone Finance
Lending.reason: Pinecone Finance is a BSC yield-aggregating auto-compounder; the exploit was a false-deposit bug in its staking-vault logic, not a money-market event.

Lending.name: Cashio
Lending.reason: Cashio issued the CASH stablecoin on Solana; the attacker bypassed collateral validation to mint unlimited CASH stablecoin, not a lending-market exploit.

Lending.name: Babylon Finance
Lending.reason: Babylon Finance was an on-chain asset-management/investment-strategy DAO (Rari user), not a permissionless money market; loss was collateral damage from Rari's Fuse hack via a strategy position.

Lending.name: Mirror Protocol
Lending.reason: Mirror Protocol is a synthetic-asset (mAsset) issuer on Terra; the long-standing vulnerability was in the synthetic-asset shorting/minting logic, which fits Derivatives (synthetic-asset issuer).

Lending.name: Whale Loans
Lending.reason: Whale Loans loss was caused by a broken K-check inside the WhaleSwap Finance AMM Pair contract; the exploited contract was the AMM pool, i.e., a DEX event.

Lending.name: Bifrost
Lending.reason: The loss originated from BiFi/Bifrost's BTC deposit-bridge server: the off-chain signing key that recognized incoming BTC was stolen, letting the attacker fake BTC deposits and pull ETH; this is a cross-chain bridge failure, not a money-market exploit.

Lending.name: Nirvana V1
Lending.reason: Nirvana Finance was an algorithmic reserve-currency / NIRV-stablecoin protocol (OHM-style with NIRV pegged stable and ANA reserve); the flash-loan attack drained the reserve liquidity pools backing the stablecoin, not a lending market.

Lending.name: Balancer
Lending.reason: Balancer disclosed the Euler contagion drained ~$11.9M from its bbeUSD boosted-pool liquidity; the loss occurred inside a Balancer AMM (DEX) LP pool, not on a lending market.

Lending.name: Idle Finance
Lending.reason: Idle Finance's loss was inside its Yield Tranches and Best Yield vaults exposed to Euler eTokens; Idle is a yield-aggregation / tranching protocol.

Lending.name: Yearn Finance
Lending.reason: Yearn Finance's loss was indirect exposure of yvUSDT/yvUSDC vaults (via Idle and Angle strategies) to the Euler hack; Yearn is a yield aggregator, not a lending market.

Lending.name: Aave Protocol
Lending.reason: A single Aave user's personal wallet was drained after a phishing attack revoked their aToken approvals; this is a wallet-phishing loss, not a protocol/lending exploit.

Lending.name: Steadefi
Lending.reason: Steadefi self-describes as an automated leveraged-yield strategy platform; a deployer-wallet compromise let attackers seize ownership of the yield vaults, so this belongs in Yield.

Lending.name: Gamma Strategies
Lending.reason: Gamma Strategies is a concentrated-liquidity asset-management/vault protocol; the exploit manipulated the Algebra AMM spot price used when depositing into its LP-vaults, i.e., a yield-vault event, not a money-market event.

Lending.name: vETH (VirtualToken)
Lending.reason: vETH exploit stemmed from a hidden factory function that let anyone inject vETH into Uniswap V2 pools, inflating x*y=k and extracting the AMM price difference; the loss vector was an AMM/DEX-pool manipulation, not a lending market.

Lending.name: AlexLab II
Lending.reason: AlexLab is Stacks' primary AMM/DEX; attacker registered a fake-transfer token via the self-listing mechanism and drained multiple AMM vault pools by creating a liquidity pool for it, i.e., a DEX/listing exploit.

Lending.name: BetterBank
Lending.reason: BetterBank's exploited component was the FAVOR-token bonus-minting system (FavorRouterWrapper) that let an attacker-created rogue LP pair trigger unlimited ESTEEM reward-token minting; despite the 'Bank' name, this is a yield-/rewards-farm mint exploit, not a money-market event.

Lending.name: Venus
Lending.reason: A single Venus user was phished via a malicious Zoom client and signed a delegate-approval transaction; the loss came from a personal-wallet phishing attack (later fully recovered), not a Venus protocol exploit.

Lending.name: UXLINK
Lending.reason: UXLINK is a decentralized-social identity project; a multisig private-key compromise let the attacker mint 1B UXLINK tokens. It is not a lending protocol at all — it is a social-app token exploit.
